overall: Round 2 established sufficient context and no blocking concern. The canonical workflow order plus ordered-subsequence validation and exact current-phase admission enforce proof before security review and security review before verification, integration, or push. Admissions bind authority, plan, mechanism, candidate, and prior gates. The controller reloads the keyed security record and raw report, re-derives the full-record key, binds the exact consumed admission, re-applies report acceptance and the non-zero-exit rule, and rejects arbitrary, stale, tampered, or replayed PASS claims. Owner-checkout drift is checked by exact pre/post candidate identity. Schema v3 rejects old workflow and plan shapes. Remaining items are verification-sufficiency gaps and risks within the disclosed same-user and trusted-toolchain boundary, not blockers.
gaps: The round-2 packet did not include the full launchguardian_report_acceptance body or test source, so some report-mapping details remained supported by deterministic suite evidence rather than peer-visible code.
The head of the command-contract validator was outside the bounded context, so the exact target-equality line was not peer-visible in round 2.
Record-time Path and revalidation-time string target normalization remained outside the peer-visible acceptance body.
The real LaunchGuardian report was supplied as an exact SHA-256 plus structural summary rather than complete bytes.

Workflow state validation converts the reviewed plan-reference and security-store failures to ControlError, but unrelated malformed authority or circuit subtrees may still raise native type/key errors.
risks: Revalidation proves the stored report target matches the stored fixed command; after the fresh proof root is deleted, a self-consistent forged record/report pair remains possible to a same-user state writer, as disclosed.
Candidate commit is stored but workflow binding is enforced primarily through the v2 executable fingerprint and exact consumed-admission digest.
The explicit owner_checkout_unchanged true value records that the runner's drift check passed; the substantive check remains the runner's pre/post exact identity comparison.
Platform path normalization differences may fail closed and make the security phase unavailable on an affected host.
A crash between raw-report storage and record storage can leave an unreferenced report artifact until cleanup.
